newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June real earnings rose 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June real earnings rose 0.5 pct.

text.p: U.S. workers' average weekly earnings, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, rose 0.5 percent in June, the Labor Department said on Wednesday.
The June increase followed a revised 0.6 percent rise in May real average weekly earnings. Previously, the department reported that May real earnings rose 0.3 percent.

The June rise reflects increases of 0.3 percent in both average hourly earnings and average weekly hours, which were partially offset by a 0.1 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, the Labor Department said.
Real average weekly earnings last month were 1.3 percent higher than the June 1996 level, the department said.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $261.42 in June, versus a revised $260.14 in May and $258.07 in June 1996.
The department had previously reported May weekly earnings at $259.60.

In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $424.03 in June, compared with a revised $421.43 in May and $409.81 in June last year. The deparment had previously reported May current dollar earnings at $420.56.
